overview.description: Every component has a hand-authored <name>.contract.json meant to be a machine-readable contract (props, anatomy, tokens, a11y, behavior rules). An audit found severe shape inconsistency across the 28 files - not just missing fields, but genuinely incompatible JSON shapes for the same field name. docs/components/registry.json is generated from these files by scripts/generate-component-registry.mjs, which normalizes every field to one canonical shape and validates the result against docs/foundations/component-registry.schema.json. This is the reliable, single-fetch, machine-consumable view; the source contract.json files remain the deep-dive reference for one component's full, un-normalized detail.
overview.purpose: Let an agent or tool query structural facts (props, anatomy, sizes, slots, variants) across many components at once without reading 28 differently-shaped files, while never fabricating content the source files don't actually contain.

classification.description: Every component is classified on two independent dimensions. They answer different questions and must not be conflated - a component's tier says nothing about its category, and vice versa.

tier.meaning: Compositional complexity - what a component is built from.
tier.source: Derived from the component's folder (packages/ui/src/components/<tier>/, docs/components/<tier>/). Not authored in contract.json.
drives: composition rules (a tier composes only from lower tiers, plus the documented exceptions in CLAUDE.md)

category.meaning: Functional / documentation grouping - the job the component does for the user.
category.allowedValues: The `category` enum in docs/foundations/component-registry.schema.json is the single authoritative list. Other files may attach definitions, labels, or ordering to those values (e.g. `categories` below), but never define the set themselves.
category.source: Authored as the top-level `category` key in each <name>.contract.json. Required: registry generation fails if it is missing or not in the schema enum.
drives: Storybook sidebar group (story titles must match - see `storybook` below)

categories.description: Definition of each category value. Keys must match the schema enum exactly - this is metadata for the values, not a second list of them.

definitions.actions: Triggers something — submits, confirms, opens, or offers a set of actions.
definitions.forms: Captures or edits a value — inputs, pickers, selection controls, and the field/form structure around them.
definitions.feedback: Communicates system status — messages, loading, progress toward completion, and empty states.
definitions.navigation: Moves the user, or shows where they are — links, wayfinding, and position within a sequence.
definitions.data-display: Presents information — metadata, people, records, and content surfaces.
definitions.overlays: Layers content above the page — dialogs, tooltips, and anchored popups.
definitions.foundations: Component-like system assets that are documented with the design foundations rather than as product UI - e.g. Icon, Focus Ring, Logo.

foundationsScope.rule: `foundations` is a valid category for component-like system assets (Icon, Focus Ring, Logo): they have a contract.json and appear in registry.json like any other component.
foundationsScope.distinction: The Foundations documentation section is broader than the category. It also holds non-component documentation - Color, Typography, Spacing, Radius, Elevation, Motion - which has no contract.json and never appears in registry.json.
foundationsScope.consequence: Filtering registry.json by `category: foundations` returns only the component-backed subset, not the complete Foundations documentation section. Don't use it as an index of foundations docs.

assignmentRules: Classify by the job the component does for the user, not by how it looks or by its tier.
Progress components: progress toward completion or an outcome -> feedback (Progress Bar). Position within a sequence or workflow -> navigation (Progress Indicator, Progress Tracker).
Behavior beats appearance: Link Button renders an <a>, so it is navigation even though it looks like a Button.
Dropdown Menu and Menu are actions - their job is offering actions. Being reused inside Select or an overflow trigger is composition, not category.
Chip edits an applied filter or property, so it is forms; Tag is display-only metadata, so it is data-display.
Inline Edit is forms - it is an input mechanism, even when it sits inside a Key Value Pair or Table cell.
Each component gets exactly one category. When a component plausibly fits two, record the deciding reason here rather than splitting it.

deferredCategories.decision: Not created yet. Card stays in data-display until there are enough real layout components (e.g. a coded Page Header) to justify a separate group - no one-item categories.

storybook.titleRule: Every component (every contract.json) has exactly one story file whose meta `title` is `Components/<group label>/<display name>`, or `Foundations/<display name>` for the `foundations` category. Titles never use the retired `UI/<Tier>/` form.
storybook.componentGroupsRule: Sidebar label and order for each component category. Must cover exactly the schema enum minus `foundations`, which is its own top-level Foundations section rather than a group under Components.
storybook.displayNameRule: The contract `name` split into words at each capital (`ProgressBar` -> `Progress Bar`), unless the name is listed in displayNameOverrides.
storybook.ordering: parameters.options.storySort in .storybook/preview.js fixes the order of top-level sections and of the component groups (which must be componentGroups' labels, in order); components sort alphabetically within a group, keeping every `X Group` next to `X` without nesting. storySort has to stay an inline literal because Storybook reads it statically, so it is a literal copy of the labels - the test below catches drift.

enforcement.test: packages/ui/src/components/component-taxonomy.test.ts (runs in `npm test`, so CI fails on drift)
fails when: a contract's category is missing or not in the schema enum
the governance category definitions or componentGroups don't cover exactly the schema enum
the storySort component-group order differs from componentGroups
a displayNameOverrides key isn't a real component name
a component has no story with its expected title, or more than one
a `Components/` story uses an unknown group or matches no contract's name and category

componentStatus.description: How ready each component is, in one of four statuses. The status is authored in each component's contract.json (`status`), and component-status.test.ts fails if it claims more than the evidence below supports. People can always set a lower status than the evidence allows (judgment: an API about to change, a design still moving); never a higher one. Decided with the owner 2026-10-19.

values.label: Draft
values.meaning: Not ready to build product screens with. It may be incomplete, change without notice, or go away.

values.label: Beta
values.meaning: Usable, documented, and tested, but it has known issues or gaps, or its API may still change. Check its known issues before relying on it.

values.label: Stable
values.meaning: Safe to build with. Complete, matched to Figma, with no known issues. A breaking change goes through a deprecated alias first (see deprecated-aliases in component-api-governance.json).

values.label: Deprecated
values.meaning: Replaced: don't use it in new work. `replacedBy` names its successor, and it's removed once nothing uses it.

criteria.label: Docs page
criteria.checkedBy: An MDX Docs page beside the component's code: on the component page standard (<ComponentHeader id>), or the component's own page (Icon's is Foundations / Icons).

criteria.label: Tests
criteria.checkedBy: A *.test.ts(x) file beside the component's code.

criteria.label: Figma source
criteria.checkedBy: contract.json has a figmaSource (any shape in design-code-mapping-governance.json, including a documented no-node exception).

criteria.label: Full contract
criteria.checkedBy: contentCompleteness is full (see contentCompleteness in this file).

criteria.label: Full examples
criteria.checkedBy: exemplarCompleteness is full in exemplars.json (see component-exemplars-governance.json).

componentStatus.knownIssues: Unresolved bugs, gaps, and open decisions about one component, as `knownIssues: [{ kind: bug | gap | decision, summary }]` in its contract.json. They hold it below Stable and show on its Docs page and the Status page. Different from knownLimitations, which are designed boundaries (a deferred feature, a documented constraint) and don't affect status. Issues that span many components or aren't about a component (tokens, Figma publishing, docs tooling) stay in docs/open-items.md.
componentStatus.deprecation: A deprecated component sets `replacedBy` to the id of the component to use instead, which must exist. Renamed props and values are not component deprecations: they stay @deprecated aliases (component-api-governance.json).
componentStatus.shownOn: The component's Docs page header (with its known issues), Introduction / Status (every component, its evidence, and what holds it back), the Overview's component counts, and a marker in Storybook's sidebar for anything not Stable.
componentStatus.implementation: scripts/lib/component-status.mjs reads these criteria; generate-component-registry.mjs records each component's evidence (statusCheck) in registry.json; component-status.test.ts recomputes it from the source tree and checks the authored status and the registry against it.

rawShapesHandled: object keyed by group -> array of strings (flattened, group preserved on each entry)
object keyed by part -> description string ({name: key, description: value})
normalizationRules.dataDropped: Button-style per-part {element, required} detail is not carried into the registry - read the source contract.json for that.
none - missing sub-fields become null/false, never a fabricated value

rawShapesHandled: object keyed by size name -> dimension detail (reduced to Object.keys())
absent - see the sizingDetail escape hatch below for the Skeleton-style free-size case
normalizationRules.dataDropped: per-size token/dimension detail (e.g. exact height/padding/radius per size) - read the source contract.json for that.

normalizationRules.canonicalShape: passthrough object, only present when the source file has a `sizing` key and no `sizes` key
normalizationRules.note: Free-size components (e.g. Skeleton) don't have a size enum - detected structurally (has sizing, lacks sizes), not by component name, so a future component reusing this pattern is handled automatically.

normalizationRules.dataDropped: per-slot supports/interactive detail - read the source contract.json for that.

rawShapesHandled: axis -> object of arbitrary per-value detail
mixed shapes across a single file's own axes (dispatched per-axis, not per-file)
normalizationRules.dataDropped: per-variant purpose/className/dimension detail - read the source contract.json for that.

normalizationRules.canonicalShape: Array<{name, anatomy, props}>, always present ([] when unused)
normalizationRules.note: Handles the Radio contract.json, which documents Radio and RadioGroup in one file, nested under radio/radioGroup keys. Detected by those keys, so its top-level anatomy (which the Docs page labels Radio's parts from) becomes the entry's anatomy without hiding the sub-components.

contentCompleteness.description: Each registry entry gets a structurally-derived contentCompleteness: full | partial | stub, based on how many of 8 near-universal substantive sections (purpose, useCases, states, accessibility, behaviorRules, do, dont, acceptanceCriteria) are present and non-empty in the source file.
contentCompleteness.purpose: Surfaces real content gaps (not shape drift) as a queryable signal instead of only living in prose a reader might skip.

knownShapeDrift.description: Contract.json files authored before this normalization convention existed may use any of the rawShapesHandled variants documented above per field. This is expected and handled automatically by the generator - it is not a per-file violations ledger (roughly 24 of 28 files deviate from a single canonical shape in at least one field, which would make an enumerated list unwieldy and low-value).
knownShapeDrift.resolution: When a component's contract.json is next substantively touched, converge its anatomy/props/sizes/slots/variants directly to the canonical shapes documented above, reducing reliance on generator-side normalization over time. Same 'migrate when next touched' philosophy as component-api-governance.json's knownViolations for Button/IconButton's isDisabled prop - applied at the shape level instead of enumerated per file.

validationApproach.rationale: One source of truth (component-registry.schema.json) instead of a second hardcoded shadow-copy of the shape in validator code. No new runtime dependency, consistent with this repo's narrowly-scoped-tooling precedent (stylelint-declaration-strict-value is a single-purpose plugin, not a general rule engine).
validationApproach.revisitThreshold: Add a real JSON Schema library (e.g. ajv) only if the schema needs features the mini-interpreter doesn't support (oneOf, $ref, conditional if/then) - not before. This is a conscious future decision point, not something to reach for preemptively.

generation.rationale: docs/components/registry.json is committed generated output, colocated with its source data - same convention as packages/ui/src/tokens/generated (Style Dictionary build output, also committed, not gitignored). Not wired into `npm run validate` or CI, matching the existing npm run generate:icons precedent (also a manual, on-demand command, not auto-run or staleness-checked in CI).
